newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN excludes 20 Rwandans from refugee status.
newsitem.headline: UN excludes 20 Rwandans from refugee status.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency announced on Tuesday it was excluding from refugee status 20 Rwandans, indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and believed to be living in Europe and Africa.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in an unusual statement, urged governments to "take the same measure" if the named Rwandans sought asylum, as they were believed to be "among those behind the execution and planning of the genocide".

The Geneva-based UNHCR oversees the 1951 U.N. Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, signed by 131 countries, which defines refugees' basic rights and sets minimum standards of treatment. The pact contains a clause providing for the exclusion of any person suspected to have committed a "crime against peace, a war crime, or a crime against humanity".
"The 20 Rwandans are believed to be among those behind the execution and planning of the genocide in which more than 500,000 Rwandans were killed," the UNHCR said in a statement.
"Some of these Rwandans are in the custody of the tribunal, including three who were arraigned in the Tanzanian town of Arusha in June. The others are known to be in Europe and Africa," it added.
It was not clear whether any of the named Rwandans were among the 1.7 million Rwandans staying in refugee camps in neighbouring Zaire and Tanzania, run by the UNHCR.
